analysis.title: Semiconductor/SPE: Implications from Teradyne's results: Inquiries from a third hyperscaler
key_insights: Teradyne reported 3Q (Jul-Sep) results on October 28. The stock was down 6% at the end of the briefing while the S&P 500 was flat.
Memory tester sales grew strongly on HBM demand, while SoC tester sales declined QoQ. Management said SoC tester sales would bottom in 3Q and grow again in 4Q.
Teradyne has entered the initial certification phase with a third major hyperscaler. This is apparently driven by customers exploring dual-vendor purchasing to reduce risk.

Teradyne aims to expand market share over the medium term, though it could take time. JPMorgan will monitor the spread of dual-vendor purchasing but does not see a major concern for Advantest's SoC tester market share at this time.

Teradyne's 3Q sales were $1,306 million (-2% QoQ) against a Bloomberg consensus of $1,269 million. Semiconductor tester sales were $1,072 million (-4% QoQ). SoC tester sales fell 20% QoQ and memory testers rose 42% QoQ.

4Q sales guidance is $1,250-1,350 million (-4% to +3% QoQ) against a Bloomberg consensus of $1,243 million. SoC tester sales are expected to recover in 4Q, while memory tester sales are expected to pull back from a strong 3Q.
Visibility has expanded from the traditional 13 weeks to several quarters out. Management said sales would likely continue growing QoQ between 4Q 2026 and 4Q 2027.
Management expects memory tester demand to keep rising significantly in CY2027, with HBM remaining the driver alongside flash memory and commodity DRAM.

Management projects ATE's share of semiconductor investment rising from 6% in 2025 to 8% in Jan-Aug 2026, versus about 4% in 2023. It made no new comment on the earlier outlook that the share would stabilize in the 7-9% range, but kept its bullish medium-term view on ATE market growth.
The CPO/SiPh tester market outlook is unchanged at about $100 million in 2026 and $300-700 million by 2028.

SoC testers have traditionally been single-vendor, and a shift to dual-vendor purchasing is underway. Teradyne says reaching second-vendor status takes 9-12 months in four steps: acquiring an opportunity to compete, developing a working solution, supplying a correlated solution, and ramping production.
After qualification there is a fast-follower phase where share rises gradually to about 30%, then a mature phase with share of 30-70%.

Teradyne has one project in the mature phase, ramping mid-2027 (first hyperscaler). It has two in the expansion phase: a GPU customer and a second hyperscaler ramping in 2H 2027. One project, the third hyperscaler, is in initial certification.

market_movers.rationale: Entered initial certification with a third hyperscaler for SoC testers, and management expects SoC sales to bottom in 3Q. The stock fell 6% on the day after the results.
Advantest (6857.T) faces possible SoC tester share loss from dual-vendor purchasing. JPMorgan does not think major concern is warranted at this time.

sector_views.rationale: Management keeps a bullish medium-term view on ATE market growth, with ATE's share of semiconductor investment rising and memory tester demand expected to keep growing in CY2027 on HBM.
